Q4=A: the API returns the deployment file CONTENTS + a generation MANIFEST as JSON; the server VALIDATES the content but writes NOTHING to disk or DB (produced transiently in-memory only); the BROWSER assembles the .zip client-side.

Q9=A: NO new backend runtime dependency (FastAPI + Python stdlib; already-present PyYAML for Compose parsing). NO new web npm dependency: client-side ZIP assembly is implemented with a dependency-free STORE-method writer (no package added, so no orchestrator ask was required).

Endpoint operates on a structured RecommendationRequest / internal ids ONLY (never a user-supplied URL): no SSRF surface. Recommendation is recomputed deterministically from the published catalogue, then deployment files are generated from the recommended architecture.
objective: Add a server endpoint POST /adviser/export that, given a structured RecommendationRequest, recomputes the deterministic recommendation and generates a deployment bundle (docker-compose.yml, .env.example, README.md, MANIFEST.json) returned as JSON = {files:[{path,content,sha256,size}], manifest:{...}}, SERVER-VALIDATED and NEVER PERSISTED (in-memory only; no file on disk, no DB row). The web SPA adds a keyboard-operable, labelled Download deployment (.zip) control on the adviser result view that fetches the validated content+manifest and assembles the .zip CLIENT-SIDE with a dependency-free STORE-method writer, offering it as a download. No secret material is ever included; env files carry ONLY .env.example placeholders. Honest Unknown; a11y throughout.

acceptance_criteria: 1. POST /adviser/export takes a structured RecommendationRequest, recomputes the deterministic recommendation, and returns JSON {files:[{path,content,sha256,size}], manifest:{...}} generated in-memory. Identical input -> byte-identical output.
2. NOT PERSISTED server-side: a probe proves no new file appears on disk and DB row counts are unchanged after a generation (fail the slice otherwise).

3. SECRET-FREE + validated fail-closed: the secret scanner rejects a planted secret; env files contain ONLY .env.example placeholders; invalid YAML, path traversal/absolute paths, oversized content, and a missing healthcheck are each REJECTED with a clear error; generated Compose parses, every service has a healthcheck, images are on a multi-arch allowlist, and amd64+arm64 is asserted.
4. No SSRF: the endpoint operates on the structured request / internal ids only; no field is fetched as a URL/host (the request schema already rejects URL-like input).

5. Web: a labelled, keyboard-operable Download deployment (.zip) control on the adviser result view fetches the validated content+manifest and assembles the .zip CLIENT-SIDE (dependency-free STORE writer); the zip contains exactly the validated files with .env.example placeholders only; no secret material is ever included. Honest Unknown; aria-live status.
6. a11y: the control is a real <button> with an accessible name, keyboard-operable, with an aria-live status region; error states use role=alert; no colour-only signalling. Asserted in tests.
7. No new backend dependency and no new web dependency; no migration (Alembic head stays 0007); requirements-sync + npm audit stay green; earlier tests stay green.

Generated content is secret-free (scanner rejects planted secrets; env files carry only .env.example placeholders). risks.immutability: No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and no DB write; the endpoint reads the published catalogue read-only and returns a pure projection.
risks.regression: Additive endpoint + additive TS types + one additive fetcher + a new zip writer + a new download component + additive CSS + additive tests. Existing routes, fetchers, and tests unchanged.
